BERTScore is a secondary metric and is structurally low here — the mandated rescale_with_baseline=True plus terse reference answers penalize correct-but-verbose text. The LLM judge (strict + graded) is primary. Absolute BERTScore matters less than the relative ordering, where GraphRAG still leads.
Citation quality (blind gpt-4o-mini judge: does the supplied evidence support the answer) is 0.000 for LLM-only by construction — no retrieval, nothing to cite. Basic RAG scores highest (0.459): it always supplies a full 10-chunk window, giving the judge more evidence to match against, at ~2× GraphRAG's tokens. GraphRAG (0.392) trades a modest citation-quality gap for provenance-sentence compression — ~35× less context on aggregation questions — while still far above the no-citation floor. GraphRAG is also the cheapest retrieval pipeline: 48% lower cost per question than Basic RAG ($0.000775 vs $0.001490), at comparable latency.

Architecture — wireframe

End-to-end system diagram: SEC filings corpus → two-phase Gemini extraction into a curated knowledge graph → TigerGraph Savanna (graph + vector store) → the three pipelines (LLM-only, Basic RAG, and the router-driven GraphRAG pipeline) → blind gpt-4o-mini judging layer. Fairness controls (same generator/embedder/context budget) constrain Pipelines 2 and 3 to isolate the graph's contribution.

The graph's advantage concentrates in Tier C (aggregation) — "which companies are audited by KPMG", "companies naming TSMC as a foundry" — where a vector RAG must scan ~100 filings and misses members, while one graph traversal returns the exact set.

Ablation — what each GraphRAG mechanism contributes

ConfigurationStrict passΔ accAvg tokensΔ tokens
Full GraphRAG46%—2359—
− graph (vector-only) 22% -24 pts 4068 +1709
− router (all-vector path) 28% -18 pts 4706 +2347
− compression (full chunks) 44% -2 pts 3192 +833
Each mechanism earns its place: removing the graph halves accuracy (0.46→0.22) and raises tokens; the router saves ~48% of tokens; compression trims ~23% at flat accuracy. Crucially, no token saving comes at an accuracy cost.

Adopted: similarity_cosine (plain cosine top-k, no MMR, no cross-encoder reranker) — beats the prior MMR+reranker baseline on strict pass, graded quality, and BERTScore simultaneously, at ~flat tokens/cost and ~12% lower latency (no reranker to run). mmr_lambda_0.7 scores marginally higher strict pass (+0.02, 1 question) but that's within single-run noise and costs nearly 2× the latency with no token benefit. Confirmed under the frozen 3-run held-out protocol: strict 0.333±0.012 vs the old baseline's 0.327±0.019 — the win holds up beyond single-run noise (see Scorecard above).
